issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (East Asia)

plan.diagnosis: Delta Allied Components Manufacturing Co. (CN) accounts for $1,486,147 in trailing 12-month spend and relies on 58 sub-tier suppliers with a single-source dependency in East Asia, creating concentration risk despite a strong resiliency score of 86 and zero disruption events in the past 12 months. The medium severity stems from geographic concentration rather than current operational weakness, requiring proactive mitigation before a geopolitical or regional supply shock materializes.

remedy_steps.step: Request full sub-tier supplier mapping from Delta Allied Components, identifying the critical single-source East Asia component(s) and current lead times, MOQs, and specifications within 30 days
remedy_steps.owner: Supplier Quality Engineer & Procurement Category Lead

remedy_steps.step: Conduct market scan to identify and pre-qualify 2-3 alternate sub-tier suppliers outside East Asia (target EMEA or Americas) capable of supplying the single-source component(s)
Negotiate with Delta Allied Components to dual-source the critical sub-tier component by Q2 2027, including contractual requirement for 40% minimum allocation to the alternate sub-tier supplier
remedy_steps.owner: Procurement Category Lead & Supplier Relationship Manager

remedy_steps.step: Establish safety stock buffer equivalent to 8 weeks of demand ($229,254 inventory value based on $1,486,147 annual spend) for critical components until dual-sourcing is operational
Implement quarterly sub-tier audits and update supplier resiliency scorecards in centralized risk system, triggering alerts if sub-tier concentration exceeds 60% in any single geography

plan.expected_impact: Mitigation of $1,486,147 annual spend exposure through geographic diversification of sub-tier sourcing, reducing single-point-of-failure risk by approximately 40-50% ($594,459 to $743,074 de-risked spend) once dual-sourcing is operational.
kpis: Sub-tier geographic concentration ratio (target: <60% from any single region by Q3 2027)
Number of qualified alternate sub-tier suppliers (target: minimum 2 by Q2 2027)
Supply continuity: days of safety stock on hand for critical components (target: 56 days minimum)
Resiliency score trend for Delta Allied Components (maintain ≥86)
Percentage of spend allocated to alternate sub-tier sources (target: 40% by Q4 2027)
risks: Delta Allied Components may resist sub-tier transparency or dual-sourcing due to margin erosion or intellectual property concerns
Alternate sub-tier suppliers may require qualification period of 6-9 months, delaying risk mitigation timeline
Safety stock buildup of $229,254 increases working capital requirements and obsolescence risk if demand patterns shift
Cost increase of 8-15% possible if alternate sub-tier suppliers lack economies of scale of incumbent East Asia source
Geopolitical escalation in East Asia (e.g., Taiwan Strait tensions) could disrupt supply before mitigation completes, resulting in production delays
erp_actions: SAP: Add source list entry (ME01) for Delta Allied Components with quota arrangement flag, enabling split allocation tracking once alternate sub-tier is qualified
SAP: Create info record (ME11) with extended lead time (+3 weeks buffer) and update safety stock levels (MD04) for materials sourced through Delta Allied Components
Coupa: Add custom supplier risk field capturing sub-tier geographic concentration percentage and set workflow alert when concentration exceeds 60% threshold
Oracle EBS: Update supplier site (AP_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL) with dual-source requirement flag and link to approved sub-tier vendor list in DFF attributes
Cross-ERP: Flag Delta Allied Components POs with 'Sub-tier Risk - Monitoring' tag in all procurement systems (SAP MM, Oracle iProcurement, Dynamics 365 SCM, NetSuite) for visibility
Coupa: Implement approval workflow requiring VP Supply Chain sign-off for any PO >$100K to Delta Allied Components until dual-sourcing confirmed operational
